t: Acronym Expansion Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Acronym Expansion Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Acronym Expansion Engine does and why archives need it. An acronym expansion engine figures out what abbreviations stand for. When it sees 'NASA' it knows it means the National Aeronautics and Space Administration — and when the same letters mean something different in a different field, it uses the surrounding text to pick the right one. Every abbreviation gets its full name, with evidence.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Acronym Expansion Engine works
title: How the Acronym Expansion Engine works
description: Overview: what the Acronym Expansion Engine does and why archives need it. Real engines mine definitions with patterns like 'National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)' and the reverse 'NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)', building a candidate table of acronym-to-expansion pairs. At expansion time each candidate is scored by context: nearby words are compared against the contexts where each expansion was seen, domain priors weight field-specific meanings, and first-use definitions in the same document win outright. The result is an expansion plus the evidence that selected it.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Acronym Expansion Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Acronym Expansion Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Acronym Expansion Engine does and why archives need it. Real engines mine definitions with patterns like 'National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)' and the reverse 'NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)', building a candidate table of acronym-to-expansion pairs. At expansion time each candidate is scored by context: nearby words are compared against the contexts where each expansion was seen, domain priors weight field-specific meanings, and first-use definitions in the same document win outright. The result is an expansion plus the evidence that selected it. Advanced engines handle nested acronyms, plural forms, and multilingual expansions, and they learn per-collection priors so a medical archive and a military archive expand the same letters differently. Quality is measured by expansion accuracy on annotated corpora with a strict rule: an expansion with no evidence must be marked unresolved rather than guessed. The limits are novel acronyms coined inside a single document — caught by the definition-pattern miner on first use — and deliberately ambiguous shorthand, which stays flagged.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
